[title] Survey Results Summary statistics Quantiles and boxplots Python/Colab Outlook Quantiles
[body] Quantiles are cutoff points that partition an ordered sample or dataset into equal-sized groups.
[body] • A median splits a sample into two: m • Two terciles split a sample into 3 groups: T1, T2 • Three quartiles split a sample into 4 groups: Q1, Q2, Q3 • Four quintiles split a sample into 5 groups: QU1, QU2, QU3, QU4 • . . . • Ninety-nine [per]centiles split a sample into 100 groups: P1, . . . , P99
[body] Prof. Oke (UMass Amherst) CEE 260/MIE 273 M1b: Summarizing Data September 10, 2026 11 / 16

novice.takeaway: Quantiles are cutoff values in ordered data that divide it into equal-sized groups, from two groups using the median up to 100 using percentiles.
novice.inferred_claim: Quantiles provide several ways to divide ordered data into equal groups.

peer.takeaway: Quantiles are ordered-data cutoff values that create equal-sized groups, with named versions including the median, terciles, quartiles, quintiles, and percentiles.
peer.inferred_claim: Use quantiles to describe an ordered dataset by equally sized partitions.

expert.takeaway: Quantiles are ordered-data cutoffs that create equal-sized groups, with median, terciles, quartiles, quintiles, and percentiles requiring one fewer cutoff than groups.
expert.inferred_claim: Use quantiles to summarize an ordered dataset by equal-probability partitions.
